event.name: MRFA Research Day
event.intro: A day of research from trainees across Mayo Clinic in Florida: two sessions of oral and rapid-fire talks, two poster sessions, and awards to close the day. Tap any talk to see the authors and send a question to the moderator.
event.fullName: Mayo Clinic Research Fellow Association (MRFA) Research Day, Florida 2026

award.title: Audience Choice Award
text: In addition to the awards determined by the judging panel, MRFA Research Day recognizes one presentation with the Audience Choice Award, selected by the attendees in Kinne Auditorium.
After each talk, select “Rate this talk” in the program or scan the code below, choose the presentation, and rate it from one to five stars. Each talk becomes available for rating when it begins.

To keep the results fair, ratings require a Mayo Clinic sign-in, only one rating per attendee per presentation is counted, and ratings by a presentation’s own authors are excluded. Voting closes at 1:30 PM, and the recipient will be announced at the Awards Ceremony at 2:15 PM. Audience ratings are separate from the judges’ evaluations.

info.a: Full oral presentations are 10 minutes each (8 in total, 4 per session). Rapid-fire presentations are 5 minutes each (14 in total, 7 per session).

info.q: How do I ask a question?
info.a: Open a talk and tap “Ask a question,” or scan the Q&A code below. In the form, pick the talk from the list (for example, “I-4 Diego Sanchez-Calderin”), type your question, and submit. The moderator reads questions during the session.
Kinne Auditorium, Mayo Clinic in Florida, Jacksonville.
Questions about the day? Contact the MRFA organizing committee.

moderators.name: Regina Castaneda
moderators.title: Chair, Mayo Clinic Research Fellow Association (MRFA), Florida
moderators.role: Postdoctoral Research Fellow, Women's Health and Internal Medicine
moderators.bio: Regina Castaneda, MD, chairs the Mayo Clinic Research Fellow Association in Florida and is a postdoctoral research fellow in women’s health and internal medicine at Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville. Her research focuses on menopause, hormone therapy, and cardiometabolic health, with a particular interest in obesity treatment for midlife women. She has led multiple first-author publications in leading journals, including The Lancet, Annals of Internal Medicine, and JAMA, and her work on hormone therapy and tirzepatide was featured by the Endocrine Society at ENDO 2025. Her honors include the New Investigator Award from The Menopause Society (2025) and the MRFA Translational Research Award.

judgesNote: The judging panel evaluates every oral and poster presentation for scientific merit, methodology, and clarity of presentation. Judges will be announced soon.
